newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Losses of S.Korean securities houses fall in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Losses of S.Korean securities houses fall in 1996.

text.p: The combined pre-tax losses posted by South Korean securities houses declined to 509.1 billion won in fiscal 1996 ending March from 591.7 billion a year earlier, the Securities Supervisory Board said on Sunday.
The securities watchdog attributed the reduced deficit to a growth in commission fees after rising stock trading volumes.
Expanding losses in bond and stock trading and an increase in financing costs caused the losses, a board statement said.
Of 34 securities houses, including a joint-venture brokerge Dongbang Peregrine Securities, 12 companies posted before-tax profits last year.

The statement said earnings from commission and underwriting businesses by securities houses rose 16.8 percent and 125.7 percent to 1.33 trillion won and 697.3 billion won respectively. But they posted a 49.6 bilion won loss in their own stock transactions.
Their assets increased by 2.38 trillion won to 27.51 trillion won at the end of March, 1997.
The statement said Daewoo Securities posted 37.8 billion won in pre-tax losses last year from a 16.9 billion pre-tax profit a year earlier.
Tongyang Securities recorded the largest before-tax deficit of 91.7 billion last year from a 46.4 billion loss a year earlier.
Before-tax profit at Shinyoung Securities was the biggest at 33.2 billion won, followed by Daishin Securities which recorded 16.6 billion won.
